metadata.title: An Improved Data Stream Summary: The Count-Min Sketch and its Applications
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.
metadata.registry_mismatch_note: Registry expected 'Space/time trade-offs in hash coding with allowable errors' (Bloom 1970). Actual paper at this path is Cormode & Muthukrishnan, 'An Improved Data Stream Summary: The Count-Min Sketch and its Applications' (2003).

nodes.name: Data stream model (turnstile / cash register)
nodes.statement: A vector $a \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with $a_i(0) = 0$ is updated by a stream of pairs $(i_t, c_t)$ via $a_{i_t}(t) = a_{i_t}(t-1) + c_t$. Cash register: $c_t \geq 0$; turnstile: $c_t$ may be negative.
nodes.statement_clean: Implicit vector updated incrementally; cash register restricts to positive updates, turnstile allows arbitrary updates.

nodes.name: Point query $Q(i)$
nodes.statement: $Q(i)$ returns an approximation of $a_i$.

nodes.name: Range query $Q(l,r)$
nodes.statement: $Q(l,r)$ returns an approximation of $\sum_{i=l}^{r} a_i$.

nodes.name: Inner product query $Q(a,b)$
nodes.statement: $Q(a,b)$ returns an approximation of $a \cdot b = \sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i b_i$.

nodes.name: Count-Min (CM) sketch
nodes.statement: A two-dimensional array $\mathrm{count}[1..d, 1..w]$ with $w = \lceil e/\varepsilon \rceil$ and $d = \lceil \ln(1/\delta) \rceil$, together with $d$ pairwise-independent hash functions $h_1,\ldots,h_d : \{1,\ldots,n\} \to \{1,\ldots,w\}$.

nodes.name: Dyadic range
nodes.statement: A dyadic range is an interval of the form $[x \cdot 2^y + 1, (x+1) \cdot 2^y]$ for non-negative integers $x, y$.

nodes.name: $\phi$-Quantiles
nodes.statement: The $\phi$-quantiles of a multiset of cardinality $\|a\|_1$ are the items of rank $k\phi\|a\|_1$ for $k=0,\ldots,1/\phi$. An $\varepsilon$-approximation accepts any item with rank between $(k\phi - \varepsilon)\|a\|_1$ and $(k\phi + \varepsilon)\|a\|_1$.

nodes.name: $\phi$-Heavy Hitters
nodes.statement: The $\phi$-heavy hitters are items $i$ with $a_i \geq \phi \|a\|_1$. An $\varepsilon$-approximation outputs any $i$ with $a_i \geq (\phi - \varepsilon)\|a\|_1$.

nodes.name: CM Sketch Update Procedure
nodes.statement: On update $(i_t, c_t)$, add $c_t$ to one cell in each row of the sketch, indexed by the hash functions.
nodes.pseudocode: For all $1 \leq j \leq d$: $\mathrm{count}[j, h_j(i_t)] \leftarrow \mathrm{count}[j, h_j(i_t)] + c_t$.

nodes.name: Point Query Estimation (non-negative case)
nodes.statement: Estimate $\hat{a}_i = \min_j \mathrm{count}[j, h_j(i)]$.

nodes.name: Point Query Estimation (general case)
nodes.statement: Estimate $\hat{a}_i = \mathrm{median}_j \mathrm{count}[j, h_j(i)]$, used when entries of $a$ may be negative.

nodes.name: Inner Product Estimation
nodes.statement: Compute $(\widehat{a \cdot b})_j = \sum_{k=1}^{w} \mathrm{count}_a[j,k] \cdot \mathrm{count}_b[j,k]$ and estimate $\widehat{a \cdot b} = \min_j (\widehat{a \cdot b})_j$ for non-negative vectors.

nodes.name: Range Query via Dyadic Decomposition
nodes.statement: Maintain $\log_2 n$ CM sketches, one per dyadic level. Decompose any range $[l,r]$ into at most $2\log_2 n$ dyadic ranges and answer each by a point query, summing the results.
input: $\log_2 n$ CM sketches over dyadic levels

nodes.name: Heavy Hitters in the Cash Register Model
nodes.statement: Maintain $\|a\|_1$ online; on each update, query the new item with the CM sketch and insert into a heap if estimate exceeds $\phi \|a(t)\|_1$. Prune heap when items fall below threshold; output remaining items at end.
output: Set of items with estimated count $\geq \phi \|a\|_1$

nodes.name: Heavy Hitters in the Turnstile Model
nodes.statement: Keep $\log n$ CM sketches over dyadic ranges and perform a parallel binary search down the hierarchy: split nodes whose estimated weight exceeds $(\phi+\varepsilon)\|a\|_1$ and recurse to leaves.

nodes.name: Quantiles in the Turnstile Model
nodes.statement: Reduce quantile finding to range-sum queries via binary search: for $1 \leq k \leq 1/\phi - 1$, find $r$ such that $\hat{a}[1,r] = k\phi \|a\|_1$, using $\log n$ CM sketches over dyadic ranges.

nodes.name: Theorem 1 (Point query, non-negative case)
nodes.statement: The estimate $\hat{a}_i$ satisfies $a_i \leq \hat{a}_i$, and with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\hat{a}_i \leq a_i + \varepsilon \|a\|_1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Bound expected collision contribution via pairwise independence, then apply Markov's inequality across $d$ rows.

nodes.name: Define indicator $I_{i,j,k}$ and bound expectation
nodes.statement: Let $I_{i,j,k} = 1$ iff $i \neq k$ and $h_j(i) = h_j(k)$. By pairwise independence, $E(I_{i,j,k}) \leq 1/w = \varepsilon/e$.

nodes.name: Bound expectation of $X_{i,j}$
nodes.statement: Let $X_{i,j} = \sum_{k=1}^{n} I_{i,j,k} a_k$. Then $\mathrm{count}[j,h_j(i)] = a_i + X_{i,j}$ and $E(X_{i,j}) \leq (\varepsilon/e)\|a\|_1$.

nodes.name: Apply Markov's inequality across $d$ rows
nodes.statement: $\Pr[\hat{a}_i > a_i + \varepsilon\|a\|_1] = \Pr[\forall j: X_{i,j} > e \cdot E(X_{i,j})] < e^{-d} \leq \delta$.

nodes.name: Theorem 2 (Point query, general case)
nodes.statement: With probability $1 - \delta^{1/4}$, $a_i - 3\varepsilon\|a\|_1 \leq \hat{a}_i \leq a_i + 3\varepsilon\|a\|_1$, where $\hat{a}_i = \mathrm{median}_j \mathrm{count}[j,h_j(i)]$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: Each count deviates by more than $3\varepsilon\|a\|_1$ with probability at most $1/8$; apply Chernoff bounds to the median of $\ln(1/\delta)$ copies.

nodes.name: Theorem 3 (Inner product)
nodes.statement: $\widehat{a \cdot b} \geq a \cdot b$ and, with probability $1 - \delta$, $\widehat{a \cdot b} \leq a \cdot b + \varepsilon \|a\|_1 \|b\|_1$.
conclusions: $a \cdot b \leq \widehat{a \cdot b} \leq a \cdot b + \varepsilon \|a\|_1 \|b\|_1$ with probability $1 - \delta$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3
nodes.statement: Decompose row product into diagonal $\sum_i a_i b_i$ plus collision terms; bound the expectation of collisions and apply Markov.

nodes.name: Corollary 1 (Join size estimation)
nodes.statement: The join size of two relations on a particular attribute can be approximated up to $\varepsilon \|a\|_1 \|b\|_1$ with probability $1 - \delta$, using space $O((1/\varepsilon) \log(1/\delta))$.
assumptions: Relations encoded as non-negative vectors $a, b$

nodes.name: Theorem 4 (Range query)
nodes.statement: $a[l,r] \leq \hat{a}[l,r]$ and, with probability at least $1 - \delta$, $\hat{a}[l,r] \leq a[l,r] + 2\varepsilon \log n \|a\|_1$.
assumptions: $\log_2 n$ CM sketches over dyadic levels

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4
nodes.statement: By Theorem 1 each component is non-underestimated; the expected additive error per dyadic estimator sums to $2 \log n (\varepsilon/e)\|a\|_1$, then Markov bounds the union over estimators.

nodes.name: Theorem 5 (Quantiles in turnstile)
nodes.statement: $\varepsilon$-approximate $\phi$-quantiles can be found with probability at least $1 - \delta$ using space $O((1/\varepsilon) \log^2(n) \log(\log(n)/(\phi\delta)))$, with insert/delete time $O(\log(n)\log(\log(n)/(\phi\delta)))$.

nodes.name: Theorem 6 (Heavy hitters, cash register)
nodes.statement: Heavy hitters can be found from a positive stream using CM sketches with space $O((1/\varepsilon) \log(\|a\|_1/\delta))$ and time $O(\log(\|a\|_1/\delta))$ per item; every item with count $\geq \phi\|a\|_1$ is output, and with probability $1-\delta$ no item with count $< (\phi-\varepsilon)\|a\|_1$ is output.
conclusions: Completeness for true heavy hitters; bounded false positives w.p. $1-\delta$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6
nodes.statement: The threshold $\phi\|a(t)\|_1$ is monotone non-decreasing, so checking estimates at each update suffices to capture every heavy hitter. Scale $\delta$ via union bound over $\|a\|_1$ queries.

nodes.name: Theorem 7 (Heavy hitters, turnstile)
nodes.statement: The divide-and-conquer algorithm uses space $O((1/\varepsilon) \log(n) \log(2\log(n)/(\delta\phi)))$ and time $O(\log(n) \log(2\log(n)/(\delta\phi)))$ per update; every item with frequency $\geq (\phi+\varepsilon)\|a\|_1$ is output, and with probability $1-\delta$ no item with frequency $< \phi\|a\|_1$ is output.
conclusions: Completeness for $(\phi+\varepsilon)$-heavy hitters; controlled false positives

nodes.name: Approximate Quantiles on Data Streams
nodes.statement: Find $\varepsilon$-approximate $\phi$-quantiles of an implicit vector $a$ presented as a stream of updates.

nodes.name: Approximate Heavy Hitters on Data Streams
nodes.statement: Output all items $i$ with $a_i \geq \phi \|a\|_1$, allowing those with $a_i \geq (\phi-\varepsilon)\|a\|_1$ as false positives.

nodes.name: Hierarchical Heavy Hitters
nodes.statement: Find all nodes in a hierarchy of depth $h$ over the items that are heavy hitters after subtracting descendants' contributions.

nodes.name: Choice of $b = e$ minimizes space
nodes.statement: Setting $w = b/\varepsilon$ and $d = \log_b(1/\delta)$ for any $b > 1$ preserves the guarantee; the space cost $(2 + e/\varepsilon)\ln(1/\delta)$ is minimized at $b = e$.

nodes.name: Hierarchical heavy hitters cost improvement
nodes.statement: Using the CM sketch reduces the turnstile-model hierarchical heavy hitters cost from $O((h/\varepsilon^2) \log(1/\delta))$ to $O((h/\varepsilon) \log(1/\delta))$ space and $O(h \log(1/\delta))$ update time.

nodes.name: Common sketch framework
nodes.statement: All considered sketches (tug-of-war, count sketch, random subset sums, CM) share form $(j,k)\text{-entry} = \sum_{i: h_k(i)=j} a_i \cdot g_k(i)$, parameterized by $w$, $d$, and the auxiliary hash family $g$.

nodes.name: Simple sketches for stream correlations
nodes.statement: Design extremely simple, practical sketches such as the CM sketch for estimating correlations between data streams and other complex aggregate functions.

nodes.name: Markov's Inequality (cited)
nodes.statement: For a non-negative random variable $X$ and $t > 0$, $\Pr[X \geq t] \leq E[X]/t$.

nodes.name: Frequency moments lower bound
nodes.statement: Approximating frequency moments $F_k(t) = \sum_i (a_i(t))^k$, the number of distinct items, and the Hamming distance between strings each require $\Omega(1/\varepsilon^2)$ space.

nodes.name: Tug-of-war sketch (cited)
nodes.statement: Sketch maintaining $\sum_i a_i \cdot g_j(i)$ with $g_j: [n] \to \{+1,-1\}$ a 4-wise independent hash family; estimates $L_2$ norm and inner products with $O((1/\varepsilon^2) \log(1/\delta))$ space.

nodes.name: Count Sketch (cited)
nodes.statement: Sketch with $w = O(1/\varepsilon^2)$, $d = O(\log(1/\delta))$, and pairwise-independent sign hash $g_j$, supporting point queries with additive error $\varepsilon \|a\|_2$.

nodes.name: Random subset sums (cited)
nodes.statement: Sketch with $w=2$, $d = (24/\varepsilon^2)\log(1/\delta)$, and $g(i)=1$, used for point and range queries.
